title: Health hotline 16263 went silent over unpaid bills, now set to return
excerpt: The free doctor helpline served 11.23 lakh people in six months but stopped on 12 November when its contract lapsed. The ministry says it will be back soon.
content:
Shastho Batayan, the government's free health hotline 16263, stopped working at 9pm on 12 November after its contract expired and was not renewed, The Daily Star reported on 17 November. The health ministry has now decided to extend the contract and expects the service to resume "within a day or two".

The line gives free consultations with doctors and guidance on ambulances. It served 11.23 lakh people between 2 May and 31 October and took about 5,000 calls a day before it shut down. It was launched in 2015.

The sector programme that paid for the service ended in June 2024. The operator, Synesis IT, says it went unpaid for about two years. By April, 22 months of bills were unpaid and more than Tk 16 crore was owed, and the company cut its staff by half. The ministry said it struggled to find money for the service under its new project-based budgeting system.

"There is no scope for shutting down this public service," said ANM Bazlur Rashid, Secretary of the Health Services Division.

Why it matters

Many NGO health workers and community volunteers send people to 16263 for advice, especially at night and in places far from a doctor. The shutdown shows how a basic service can stop when a donor-style programme ends and nothing replaces it in the regular budget. The same risk hangs over other services that were built inside the old health sector programme.

What to watch

Whether the hotline is back in service this week, whether the unpaid bills are settled, and whether the ministry moves the service into its regular budget rather than short contract extensions.
